groups.title: The Three Pillars
groups.question: Explain the different kinds of telemetry a system produces and how observability differs from classic monitoring.

followUps.Metrics, Logs, and Traces: Why is it a mistake to try to get every insight from just one signal type, like only logs?
followUps.Observability vs. Monitoring: What does it mean to debug an unknown unknown, and why do fixed dashboards struggle with it?

groups.title: Monitoring Methodologies
groups.question: Walk through how you would decide what to measure first for a service and for the machines it runs on.

followUps.RED Method: How does using the same three request signals on every service help you find where latency enters a call chain?
followUps.USE Method: Why is saturation of a resource like a disk or CPU dangerous even before users see errors?

groups.title: Black-Box and White-Box Monitoring
groups.question: Explain how monitoring from outside a system differs from monitoring from inside it, and why you would want both.

followUps.Black-Box Monitoring: What kind of problem would a synthetic probe catch that your internal health checks would miss?
followUps.White-Box Monitoring: Why does internal instrumentation help you explain why something is slow and not just that it is slow?

groups.title: Incident Response Metrics
groups.question: Explain how teams measure their incident response and how observability changes those numbers.

followUps.MTTD – Mean Time to Detect: What makes the time to detect a problem long in some setups, and how would you shorten it without flooding people with alerts?
followUps.MTTR – Mean Time to Resolve: How does having metrics, logs and traces linked together shorten the time it takes to restore service?
